article_content: At the University of Buckingham, many younger classmates barely noticed 91-year-old student Bertie Gladwin quietly working on his Master of Military Intelligence degree. He did not go to the typical freshman events or take part in late-night outings, yet he proved it is never too late to succeed by earning top marks. Despite leaving school at 14, he pursued a career in the secret service and returned to academics long after retirement. He showed up for classes on campus, navigating hallways among students in their twenties, often discovering he was the oldest one in the room. Initially, he struggled with computer skills, accidentally deleting entire papers, but persevered thanks to his extensive background in intelligence work. Before this accomplishment, he had already completed a BA in Psychology and a BSc in Microbiology through the Open University, both after leaving the workforce. Mr Gladwin proudly recalls his early days: delivering groceries at 14, joining the RAF at 19, and eventually serving in World War II as a radio operator in the Middle East. Upon his return, he maintained global communications for MI6, refining the same expertise he later studied at university. Graduating just before turning 91, he credits his wife Wendy for encouraging his late-blooming education and possibly spurring him to aim for a PhD. Reflecting on his journey, he says he hopes he changed his classmates views on older learners while inspiring people of every generation to keep striving and studying.

Aunque dejó la escuela a los 14 años, siguió una carrera en el servicio secreto y regresó a la academia mucho después de jubilarse. Asistía a clases en el campus, recorriendo pasillos con compañeros de poco más de veinte años, y a menudo se daba cuenta de que era la persona de mayor edad en el aula. Al principio, tuvo dificultades con la tecnología y borró documentos enteros sin querer, pero perseveró gracias a su larga experiencia en el área de inteligencia. Antes de este logro, ya había obtenido una licenciatura en Psicología y otra en Microbiología a través de la Open University, ambas después de retirarse de su vida laboral activa. El señor Gladwin recuerda con orgullo sus inicios: entregando víveres a los 14, uniéndose a la RAF a los 19 y finalmente sirviendo en la Segunda Guerra Mundial como operador de radio en Oriente Medio. Tras su regreso, trabajó en el mantenimiento de comunicaciones globales para el MI6, profundizando en las mismas aptitudes que más tarde estudiaría en la universidad. Se graduó poco antes de cumplir 91 años y atribuye a su esposa Wendy la motivación para retomar sus estudios tarde, e incluso contempla la posibilidad de un doctorado. Al reflexionar sobre su trayectoria, señala que espera haber cambiado la percepción de sus compañeros sobre los estudiantes mayores y que su experiencia motive a todas las generaciones a seguir adelante aprendiendo.

article_content: (CNN) -- Margaret Thatcher, serving as prime minister for 11½ years, did little to elevate other women in politics. Despite that, she became a prominent figure simply because she was a woman commanding the highest office in Britain. My son was five when she first took office, and by the time she left, he was 17, having grown up with no memory of a male prime minister. As a feminist who opposed many of Thatcher's policies, I still grapple with how to feel about her. She rarely promoted women's rights actively, yet an entire generation found it normal to see a woman in the role of prime minister. During her tenure, I interviewed Sir Bernard Weatherill, then Speaker of the House of Commons, who shared a story about his grandchildren, around eight and eleven. While they dressed in the Speaker's robes, 'playing Parliaments,' his grandson said, 'I'll pretend to be prime minister,' only to be told by his granddaughter, 'Don't be silly, I'm going to be the prime minister — only women can be prime ministers!' Such was Thatcher's impact that for weeks after her departure, the media occasionally slipped and referred to her successor, John Major, as 'she' or 'her' by habit. In the early 1980s, I founded the all-party 300 GROUP campaign to elect more women. We created 43 branches across England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. Thatcher attended some 300 GROUP events and expressed support for having more women in Parliament. At an event honoring Nancy Astor, the first woman MP to take her seat, she even called the House of Commons 'a dreadfully male-dominated place.' Yet these sentiments were exceptions for her. She appointed only one other woman to her Cabinet, and only briefly. With her strong command of the Conservative Party, Thatcher could have advanced many qualified women into public office but chose not to do so. Once, former Prime Minister Edward Heath, who despised Thatcher, invited me to lunch along with pop singer Bob Geldof and several others. Heath refused to say Thatcher's name, calling her 'that woman.' At one point, he turned to me and said, 'I tell you one thing, Lesley: you'll never see another woman prime minister in this country in your lifetime after that woman.' Thatcher triggered intense emotions, presiding over a divisive era in British politics. Social media reactions to her death were a Molotov cocktail of opinions, with vitriol and misogynist language from people who otherwise seemed reasonable. She famously quoted the Prayer of St Francis after her 1979 election victory, which includes the line 'Where there is discord, may we bring harmony.' In reality, she often did the opposite. Still, as with Confucius, it may be 'too soon to tell' what her ultimate legacy will be. All opinions expressed in this commentary belong solely to Lesley Abdela.
translated_content: (CNN) -- Margaret Thatcher, quien fue primera ministra durante 11 años y medio, hizo poco para elevar a otras mujeres en la política. Aun así, se convirtió en una figura destacada simplemente por ser una mujer al mando de la posición más alta en Gran Bretaña. Mi hijo tenía cinco años cuando ella asumió el cargo por primera vez, y cuando se fue, él tenía 17, habiendo crecido sin recordar a un primer ministro hombre. Como feminista que se opuso a muchas de las políticas de Thatcher, todavía me cuesta definir mis sentimientos hacia ella. Rara vez promovió activamente los derechos de las mujeres, aunque toda una generación se acostumbró a ver normal que hubiera una mujer como primera ministra. Durante su mandato, entrevisté a Sir Bernard Weatherill, entonces presidente de la Cámara de los Comunes, quien me contó una anécdota sobre sus nietos, de alrededor de ocho y once años. Mientras se ponían la túnica del presidente y jugaban a ser parlamentarios, su nieto dijo: 'Fingiré ser el primer ministro', solo para que su nieta respondiera: 'No seas tonto, yo seré la primera ministra — ¡solo las mujeres pueden ser primeras ministras!' Tal fue el impacto de Thatcher que durante semanas después de su salida, los medios se equivocaron ocasionalmente y se refirieron a su sucesor, John Major, como 'ella' o 'su', por costumbre. A principios de la década de 1980, fundé la campaña multipartidista 300 GROUP para elegir a más mujeres. Creamos 43 filiales en Inglaterra, Escocia, Gales e Irlanda del Norte. Thatcher asistió a algunas actividades de 300 GROUP y expresó su apoyo a tener más mujeres en el Parlamento. En un evento en honor a Nancy Astor, la primera mujer diputada en ocupar su escaño, incluso describió la Cámara de los Comunes como un 'lugar terriblemente dominado por hombres'. Sin embargo, tales comentarios fueron excepciones en ella. Nombró solo a otra mujer para su Gabinete, y solo de forma breve. Con su fuerte control del Partido Conservador, Thatcher podría haber promocionado a muchas mujeres calificadas a cargos públicos, pero eligió no hacerlo. En una ocasión, el ex primer ministro Edward Heath, quien la detestaba, me invitó a comer junto con el cantante de pop Bob Geldof y otros. Heath se negó a mencionar a Thatcher por su nombre, refiriéndose a ella como 'esa mujer'. En cierto momento, se dirigió a mí y dijo: 'Te digo una cosa, Lesley: nunca volverás a ver a otra mujer primera ministra en este país en tu vida después de esa mujer.' Thatcher desencadenó emociones intensas, presidiendo una era divisiva en la política británica. Las reacciones en redes sociales tras su muerte fueron un cóctel molotov de opiniones, con expresiones de odio y lenguaje misógino por parte de personas que de otro modo parecerían razonables. Famosamente, citó la Oración de San Francisco tras su victoria electoral en 1979, que incluye la frase: 'Donde haya discordia, que llevemos armonía'. En realidad, a menudo logró lo contrario. Aun así, como con Confucio, quizás sea 'demasiado pronto para decirlo' cuál será su legado definitivo. Todas las opiniones expresadas en este comentario pertenecen únicamente a Lesley Abdela.

article_content: 'Al Qaeda has unveiled a polished propaganda video accusing President Barack Obama of responsibility for the recent deaths of an American and a South African hostage in Yemen. In the video, top AQAP commander Nasr bin Ali al-Ansi denounces Obama's rescue efforts, labeling them reckless, and warns the United States against any future hostage rescue missions.' 'Luke Somers, originally from the UK but an American citizen, and Pierre Korkie from South Africa lost their lives when U.S. special forces raided an Al Qaeda hideout last week. Al-Ansi's remarks are the first public statement by Al Qaeda following the failed attempt to rescue the two men.' 'The six-minute clip, produced by Al Qaeda's Al-Malahem media center, appears extremely polished, using HD filming techniques similar to ISIS propaganda videos from Syria and Iraq. Circulated via social media, it reveals a clear improvement in technical quality compared to earlier, lower-resolution releases by Al Qaeda.' 'In front of a dark backdrop decorated with the group’s flag, al-Ansi alleges Obama's decisions forced events down a path Al Qaeda did not intend, calling the raid an 'execution order.' Obama stated he authorized the mission because Somers, a 33-year-old journalist, was in imminent danger. Officials confirm 40 American special forces participated, alongside Yemeni troops, but were detected by militants before reaching the hostages.' 'Al-Ansi also claims the group wanted to bargain for the release of detainees at Guantanamo Bay and specifically named Sheik Omar Abdel-Rahman. He criticizes the U.S. for not negotiating and insists Al Qaeda will continue targeting Americans wherever possible.' 'Separately, Al Qaeda issued a critique of ISIS's brutal beheading videos, calling them counterproductive to the broader extremist cause. Al-Ansi vowed any future executions would involve firearms rather than beheadings, a clear reference to ISIS's notoriously gruesome recordings of captive beheadings in Syria and Iraq.'

Compartido en redes sociales, evidencia un aumento en la calidad técnica respecto a lanzamientos previos de Al Qaeda.' 'Ante un fondo oscuro con la bandera del grupo, al-Ansi acusa a Obama de haber provocado un desenlace que el grupo no deseaba, definiendo la incursión como una ‘orden de ejecución’. Obama justificó la operación al señalar que Somers, periodista de 33 años, se hallaba en peligro inminente. 'Por otro lado, Al Qaeda criticó los violentos videos de decapitación de ISIS, considerándolos dañinos para su imagen global. Al-Ansi aseguró que, en futuras ejecuciones, recurrirán a armas de fuego en lugar de decapitaciones, en clara alusión a los brutales asesinatos filmados por ISIS en Siria e Irak.'

article_content: Jake Keating, 20, from Liverpool, discovered a wasp in his Cadbury Dairy Milk bar after purchasing it in the city center last week. The construction management student at Liverpool John Moores University kept the bar, took a photo, and contacted Cadbury. He said, 'When I unwrapped the bar, I found a whole wasp inside, complete with wings and a sting.' Concerned about potential harm, he saved the bar for evidence. Cadbury asked for the bar to be returned for investigation. A Cadbury spokesperson stated, 'This certainly sounds unpleasant for Mr. Keating, and we have asked for the bar to be returned to us. Once we have the bar back, we will investigate to see where and when this could have occurred.' Dairy Milk was first introduced in Britain in 1905 and contains 23 per cent cocoa solids. Two months ago, a couple named Chris and Hayley Rice discovered a live fly buzzing inside a sealed bowl of mashed potatoes they had purchased from a Sainsbury's store in West Green, near Crawley, West Sussex. Last June, a 21-year-old man named Alex Moughton bought a BLT sandwich from a Co-op petrol station in Hopton, near Great Yarmouth, Norfolk, and found a lump of old chewing gum inside. He said he felt sick after biting into it.

Una vez que la tengamos, investigaremos para determinar dónde y cuándo pudo haber ocurrido este problema.' Dijo que se sintió enfermo después de morderlo.

article_content: Warner Bros Discovery’s international restructuring continues with James Gibbons outlining the shape of his Asia Pacific team, while Japanese Country Manager Masami Takahashi plans to retire. Last month, longtime WBD executive Gibbons was appointed President of Asia Pacific and has now revealed a new leadership structure. Reporting to him are regional chiefs Tony Qiu, Arjun Nohwar, Magdalene Ew, Lynn Ng, Shonali Bedi, and Jae Chang. Takahashi, WBD Japan Country Manager and Head of Studios, has decided to retire and will exit at the end of 2024. Recruitment for a Tokyo-based replacement will commence soon. Qiu will serve as General Manager for Greater China & Southeast Asia, overseeing Southeast Asia, Mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan. Nohwar will be GM for South Asia, based in Mumbai. Ew becomes Head of Content for Streaming in APAC, while Ng is Head of Content for Networks in APAC. Bedi is Head of Strategy, Partnerships & Insights for APAC, and Chang takes on the role of Head of Content Licensing for Southeast Asia, India, and Korea. Most of the team will be based in Singapore, except for Nohwar in Mumbai. Daniel Tan is expanding his remit to become Head of Marketing for APAC and will continue to report to Patrizio Spagnoletto, WBD’s Global Chief Marketing Officer for Direct-to-Consumer. Kurt Rieder continues as Head of Theatrical Distribution for APAC, reporting to Andrew Cripps, President of International Theatrical Distribution. Jason Monteiro remains APAC Lead for Streaming, reporting to JB Perrette, CEO and President of Global Streaming and Games. Gibbons stated, ‘Culturally, demographically, and economically, APAC is the most diverse region, with more than half of the world’s population and a mix of developed and emerging markets. There are significant growth opportunities here, and I have every confidence that this leadership and our talented teams have the expertise, skills, and ambition to drive optimum value across our globally renowned portfolio.’ He was promoted to oversee all of APAC last month in a restructure that followed several C-suite exits within WBD’s international business. Clement Schwebig, who previously managed India, Southeast Asia, and Korea, has expanded his remit to Germany, Switzerland, Austria, France, Benelux, and Africa, merging Western Europe and Africa under his leadership.

article_content: Roughly one hundred activists carrying the bodies of deceased animals convened in Melbourne, Australia, to protest violence and neglect toward animals. Members of Animal Liberation Victoria (ALV) stood silently, holding dead sheep, pigs, kangaroos, chickens, fish, and ducks, asserting they wanted to highlight the "hidden suffering" of animals in Australia and across the globe. According to ALV, the remains were recovered by their rescue team, and many of these animals had died or were dying in industrial facilities, fields, or after being hit by vehicles. Photographs from the protest show a man holding a dead chicken and a woman cradling a penguin as part of the demonstration, which aimed to call attention to the extent of animal suffering. ALV characterizes the harsh treatment of animals as among "the world's largest social justice issues," pointing to similar memorial demonstrations in Spain, Chile, France, Germany, and Peru. ALV campaign coordinator Noah Hannibal stated that humans slaughter about 64 billion land animals each year and between one and three trillion sea animals globally. Founded in 1978 by Patty Mark in Melbourne, Animal Liberation Victoria operates with goals to abolish the property status of animals, end animal exploitation, and fight attitudes and practices rooted in speciesism. The group also promotes animal rights education, endorses non-violence, and has protested against sheep exports, whaling, animal killings on television by Jamie Oliver, and deaths in Melbourne Zoo. In 1993, ALV formed the Action Animal Rescue Team to save neglected and suffering animals from factory farms.

Según ALV, los restos fueron recuperados por su equipo de rescate, y muchos de estos animales habían muerto o estaban muriendo en instalaciones industriales, campos o después de ser atropellados por vehículos. Fotografías de la protesta muestran a un hombre sosteniendo un pollo muerto y a una mujer que cargaba un pingüino, como parte de la manifestación que buscaba ilustrar la magnitud del sufrimiento animal. ALV describe el trato cruel a los animales como una de "las problemáticas de justicia social más grandes del mundo" y señala demostraciones conmemorativas similares en España, Chile, Francia, Alemania y Perú. El coordinador de campaña de ALV, Noah Hannibal, afirmó que los seres humanos sacrifican alrededor de 64 mil millones de animales terrestres cada año y entre uno y tres billones de animales marinos en todo el mundo. Fundada en 1978 por Patty Mark en Melbourne, Animal Liberation Victoria tiene como objetivos abolir el estatus de propiedad de los animales, terminar con su explotación y combatir actitudes y prácticas fundamentadas en el especismo. El grupo también promueve la educación sobre los derechos de los animales, respalda la no violencia y ha protestado contra la exportación de ovejas, la caza de ballenas, la matanza de animales en televisión por parte de Jamie Oliver y las muertes en el Zoológico de Melbourne. En 1993, ALV formó el Action Animal Rescue Team para salvar a los animales descuidados y que sufren en granjas industriales.
